info.description: REST API of the Shelf service.
info.title: Shelf API

get.description: Returns the wrapped keys: the client needs them after a restart while the access token is still alive.

post.description: Verifies auth_hash and returns the wrapped keys together with a token pair.
Revokes the session the refresh token belongs to.
Accepts the master key re-encrypted with the new wrapping key. All sessions are revoked and the response carries a new token pair.

Returns the salt and the KDF parameters the client needs to compute auth_hash.
For an unknown login it returns plausible values so the endpoint does not reveal whether the account exists.
Sets the new authentication data using the token issued by recovery/start.

Verifies ownership of the recovery code and returns the master key wrapped with it
together with a short-lived token for completing the recovery.
Exchanges a refresh token for a new pair. The token is single-use: presenting it again revokes all sessions.

Creates an account from the cryptographic material prepared by the client and opens a session.
The server never sees the password: the client derives the master key wrapping key and auth_hash from it.

get.description: Returns 200 while the process is alive. Does not check external dependencies.
Checks that PostgreSQL is reachable. Returns 503 if the database is unavailable.

token_hash.description:
TokenHash is the digest of a code the server never sees. Exactly one of this and
TargetUserID is set.

wrapped_preview.description:
Preview holds the vault name and the inviter, encrypted under the same code, so an
unauthenticated lookup reveals nothing.

key_grants.description:
Keys must cover the node's scope whenever the permission allows reading: without
them the subject would see an entry it can never open.

wrap_algorithm.description:
Algorithm names the wrapping format. Invite keys use a code-derived symmetric key
rather than a sealed box, because nobody knows yet whose key to seal to.

recovery_auth_hash.description: AuthHash is derived by the client from the recovery code and serves as the verifier.

cursor.description: Cursor is the id to pass as before= for the next page; zero when the log is exhausted.

full_resync_required.description:
FullResync tells the client to drop its cached copy of this vault. It is the only
way it learns to forget plaintext it cached before losing access to it.

key_scope_client_id.description:
KeyScopeClientID is what a sealed key names. Sealing against the vault's own client
id instead produces a key that silently refuses to open.

key_scope_id.description:
KeyScopeID and KeyVersion declare which key the blobs were sealed under. The server
refuses them when they do not match the destination, because the row would be
unreadable to everyone who can see it.

client_id.description:
ClientID is chosen before the row exists, so the metadata can be sealed against a
stable identity in one round trip.

scope_client_id.description: ScopeClientID names the vault's own key scope, which the key below is sealed against.

wrap_algorithm.description: Algorithm names the sealed-box format, so a later format can be told apart.

wrapped_key.description: WrappedKey is the vault content key sealed to the creator's own public key.

new_scope_client_id.description:
NewScopeClientID names the scope the new key belongs to. It is required when the job
creates a scope, because the sealed keys have to name it before the row exists.
